hypothesis: The post-snapshot episode-tic stability check in the pinned scorer checkpoint candidate accepts non-integer endpoint reads when Python equality aliases them to the integer acknowledged endpoint.
test: Execute pinned candidate code with three controlled stubs: integer 10→11 with integer readback 11; same endpoints with float readback 11.0; and 0→1 with boolean readback True. Retain candidate status and private log row for each case. Independent auditor validates raw case identities/statuses and source bytes without importing candidate code.
decision: FAIL_OPEN_ENDPOINT_TYPE if either malformed float or bool readback gets REFRESH_RETURNED_RUNTIME_QUALIFICATION_PENDING; PASS_FAIL_CLOSED if valid int is pending and both malformed readbacks are UNKNOWN with no values; HOLD for source mismatch, malformed raw, or auditor failure.
competing_explanation: The real ViZDoom API may always return an integer. This test targets defensive contract behavior and does not establish an observed live API type violation.
uncertainty: Small deterministic stubs against a non-integrated candidate on a PR branch. No actual game, scorer, X server, model, GUI, input, task progress, or recovery behavior is measured.
